timeline.when.at: Wrapper for a time of day; {t} is already a formatted clock time (or the when.other_day message). Keep it as just {t}.
timeline.when.other_day: A time on another day than today: {weekday} is a short weekday name (Mon..Sun), {t} the clock time. Example: Thu 6:30 AM.
timeline.weekday.mon: Short weekday name used before a clock time (Mon 6:30 AM). Use the form the language uses in a calendar header.
timeline.mode.heat: Lower-case day-plan word used inside a sentence: the day plan changes from heat to cool.
timeline.mode.off: Lower-case day-plan word used inside a sentence: neither heating nor cooling is planned that day.
timeline.occupancy.away: Lower-case word inside a sentence: the away band / the vacation band.
timeline.fan.whole_house_fan: A whole-house fan (an attic or ceiling fan that pulls air through open windows), used inside a sentence.
timeline.fan.hvac_fan: The furnace/air-handler blower fan of the HVAC system, used inside a sentence.
timeline.sensor.bedroom: The bedroom temperature sensor (a room sensor), used after 'reads the'.
timeline.sensor.thermostat: The thermostat's own temperature reading, used after 'reads the'.
timeline.step.wake_band.default: CA = Climate Advisor. {t} is the time (it may carry a weekday). The comfort band is the allowed temperature range, {floor} to {ceiling}.
timeline.step_short.wake_band.default: Row text in the 'Next 24 hours' list; the time and a 'CA' badge are shown in their own columns, so the sentence starts with the verb. Capitalise the first word.
timeline.step.windows_open.free_cooling: An instruction to the occupant (open the windows). {delta} is a temperature difference, {end} the time the window period is expected to end.
timeline.step.summary.windows_open: Keep the (s) of 'period(s)': it stands for a plural-neutral count. {hours} is a number of hours; keep the 'h' unit abbreviation.
timeline.step.run.heat: A prediction: heating is expected to run for about {minutes} minutes in the given interval to keep the temperature at {edge}.
timeline.step.held.suffix: {base} is a complete earlier sentence; this one is appended after it. {until} is a time.
timeline.step.held.pause: {base} is a complete earlier sentence; this one is appended after it.
timeline.card.open_at: Short card text telling the occupant when to open the windows; no final period.
timeline.card.open_briefly: The windows should be opened for a short time because outdoor air is warmer than indoor and the house is cold.
timeline.next_automation.briefing_send: A card label for the next thing the automation will do: send the daily briefing notification. No time in the label; no final period.
timeline.next_automation.sleep_band.heat: Setback = lowering the heating target at bedtime; {temp} is the new target.
timeline.next_automation.tou_bank_end: TOU = time-of-use electricity pricing. {after} is a short phrase already written in this language (what the thermostat returns to).
timeline.strip.run_heat_placed: Hover text on a chart bar: heating is expected to run for about {minutes} minutes between two times, holding the lower edge (floor) of the comfort band.
timeline.v4.unusable_fit: v4 is a forecasting model. 'refit' = the model was re-trained on the latest data; {reason} is a short reason, {kept} a date (YYYY-MM-DD) or the phrase 'an earlier fit'.
timeline.v4.mode.starts: 'starts' = thermostat heating/cooling cycles that began; {acc} usable of {tot} total.
timeline.v4.by_mode: Two mode summaries separated by a middle dot; keep the separator.
timeline.v4.node.headline_rooms: {changed} selects 'now forecasts' (the model just switched) or 'forecasts'.
timeline.v4.node.score_room: {b} and {a} are average forecast errors (temperature differences); {more} is 'none' or 'some'; {others} is a parenthesised list of other lead times.
timeline.v4.node.others_two: Average forecast error at two other lead times (hours ahead): '1 h 0.4°F vs 0.5°F, 12 h 0.8°F vs 0.9°F'.
